unclear.text: The research found no documented position of the party on this issue, so it can't be compared with your answer.

emergency-powers-shin-bet.text: That is the party's documented approach: on 15 July 2026 the government approved a plan, led by Benjamin Netanyahu, Social Equality Minister May Golan and National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir, to bring the Shin Bet into the fight against crime organisations in Arab society, and in June 2023 the party published a bill for holding people considered a danger to the public without trial. That bill did not limit its scope by community, though at the time Ben Gvir opposed using such detention against Jewish suspects.

more-police-resources-normal-law.text: The party's documented approach is different, because it relies on special powers: on 15 July 2026 the government approved bringing the Shin Bet into the fight against crime organisations, and on 19 October 2025 a ministerial committee approved a party bill letting the National Security Minister declare a crime organisation a terror organisation.

invest-in-arab-communities-first.text: The party's documented approach is different: under a plan led by Benjamin Netanyahu, Social Equality Minister May Golan and National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir, the government on 15 July 2026 moved about NIS 497 million out of the five-year development plan for Arab society to a Shin Bet unit and a national police unit. The coalition agreement committed to revising that development plan, with emphasis on personal security, law and order, and youth employment.

resume-fighting-full-control.text: That is the party's documented position: all its ministers voted against the government's ceasefire and hostage deal on the night of 9-10 October 2025, and in September 2026 it published a plan to encourage Gaza residents to emigrate voluntarily. In October 2024 National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir also said Israel can renew the settlements in Gaza.

hold-positions-disarmament-first.text: The party shares your opposition to relying on international forces: on 30 September 2025 National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir objected that the US plan withdraws the IDF from operational control of Gaza and hands security to international forces. But it wants fighting against Hamas to resume until total victory and supports voluntary emigration and Jewish settlement in Gaza, which go beyond holding current positions.

advance-international-arrangement.text: The party opposes this plan: all its ministers voted against the government's ceasefire and hostage deal on the night of 9-10 October 2025, and on 30 September 2025 National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir called the US plan dangerous to Israel's security.

end-war-full-withdrawal.text: The party wants the opposite: in January 2025 its three ministers resigned from the government over the earlier ceasefire and hostage deal, and they returned about two months later, when fighting in Gaza resumed. After a July 2026 announcement of a deal for Hamas to disarm, National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir called for military operations in Gaza to continue.

defeat-hamas-then-security-control.text: The party shares your call to go back to war until Hamas is defeated: after a July 2026 announcement of a deal for Hamas to disarm, National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir called for military operations in Gaza to continue. It differs on the second half of your answer, because its September 2026 plan encourages Gaza residents to emigrate voluntarily and Ben Gvir has said Israel can renew the settlements in Gaza.

anchor-torah-study-exemption.text: The party's documented approach is different: its stated aim is to integrate Haredim into service, and in a September 2026 Ynet survey of parties' enlistment plans National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir described dedicated police and Border Police tracks for Haredim that preserve Shabbat, kashrut, prayer and Torah study. It does share your opposition to coercion: on 28 October 2024 Ben Gvir said the party believes in enlistment in the army, but not in coercion.

gradual-targets-by-agreement.text: The research places the party closest to your answer, but with mixed evidence: in a September 2026 Ynet survey National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir emphasised agreement with rabbis and frameworks suited to Haredim, such as police and Border Police tracks. The research found no source showing the party supporting enlistment targets or funding cuts, and the party's published response did not mention sanctions or quotas.

universal-service-with-sanctions.text: The party shares your support for military service: on 28 October 2024 National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir said it believes in enlistment in the army. But he added that it is not for coercion, and the party's published response to a September 2026 Ynet survey did not mention sanctions or enlistment quotas.

voluntary-service-for-all.text: This is a secondary element of the party's position: on 28 October 2024 National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir said he does not think coercion will help to make a Haredi enlist and that benefits for reservists should come first. He did not apply this to service in general, and said the party believes in enlistment in the army.

speed-up-planning-and-construction.text: The research found no general housing-price platform from the party, so no documented position on what this option proposes. The limited evidence points elsewhere: new communities in the Negev and Galilee through the ministry of Yitzhak Wasserlauf, Minister for the Negev, Galilee and National Resilience, expanded in February 2023.

state-led-affordable-rental.text: The research found no general housing-price platform from the party, so no documented position on what this option proposes. The limited evidence points elsewhere: new communities in the Negev and Galilee through the ministry of Yitzhak Wasserlauf, Minister for the Negev, Galilee and National Resilience, expanded in February 2023.

direct-help-for-buyers.text: This is a secondary element of the party's position, resting on limited evidence: the party's September 2026 plan for the Defence Ministry includes free land for combat soldiers, which resembles the help for those who served in your answer. The research found no general housing-price platform from the party.

develop-periphery-and-transport.text: This is a secondary element of the party's position, resting on limited evidence: in February 2023 the government expanded the ministry of Yitzhak Wasserlauf to cover the Negev and Galilee, and in May 2023 the party obtained an extra NIS 250 million for it. The party's documented actions there focus on new communities, and the research found no general housing-price platform from the party.

military-pressure-until-threats-removed.text: That is the party's documented position, shown in statements: on 15 June 2026 National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir wrote that Israel must not settle for anything less than the dismantling of Hezbollah and must not withdraw from a single inch of territory the IDF captured in Lebanon, and on 4 June 2026 he called the US-brokered Lebanon ceasefire a serious mistake.

force-plus-us-backed-agreements.text: The party shares your emphasis on military pressure, but it has opposed US-brokered deals that stop short of dismantling Hezbollah: on 15 June 2026 National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir wrote that the US-Iran agreement does not bind Israel, and on 4 June 2026 he called the US-brokered Lebanon ceasefire a serious mistake and said Israel must know how to say no, even to the US president.

prioritize-ending-multifront-war.text: The party holds the opposite order of priorities: on 22 June 2026 National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir warned against another weak ceasefire, and on 4 June 2026 he called the US-brokered Lebanon ceasefire a serious mistake.

end-military-operations-regional-peace.text: The party holds the opposite position: on 15 June 2026 National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir wrote that Israel must not withdraw from a single inch of territory the IDF captured in Lebanon, and in October 2024 he said the party demands total victory in the north, in Gaza and against Iran.

full-sovereignty.text: That is the party's documented position: on 22 October 2025 all six of its MKs who voted supported a bill to apply Israeli sovereignty to Judea and Samaria, which passed a preliminary reading by 25 to 24. The research found no source showing the party's position on dismantling the Palestinian Authority.

partial-sovereignty-area-c.text: The party shares part of your answer, with a mixed voting record: on 22 January 2025, days after it left the government, all six of its MKs who voted supported a bill to apply Israeli sovereignty to the Jordan Valley, but on 31 December 2025, back in the coalition, its five MKs who voted opposed an opposition bill to apply it to Beitar Illit. Its documented aim is to apply sovereignty to Judea and Samaria as a whole.

maintain-current-situation.text: The party holds a different position: it aims to apply Israeli sovereignty to Judea and Samaria, and on 22 October 2025 all six of its MKs who voted supported a bill to do so.

separation-two-states.text: The party opposes a Palestinian state and aims to apply Israeli sovereignty to Judea and Samaria: on 22 October 2025 all six of its MKs who voted supported a bill to do so. On 6 September 2026 National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir said a Palestinian state would be an existential threat and that he is prepared to absorb sanctions to prevent it.

two-states-pre-1967-border.text: The party opposes a Palestinian state and aims to apply Israeli sovereignty to Judea and Samaria: on 22 October 2025 all six of its MKs who voted supported a bill to do so. On 6 September 2026 National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir said a Palestinian state would be an existential threat and that he is prepared to absorb sanctions to prevent it.

one-equal-state.text: The party's documented position is different: according to the Israel Democracy Institute its ideology supports the whole Land of Israel and applying Israeli sovereignty to Judea and Samaria, and on 22 October 2025 all six of its MKs who voted supported a bill to apply that sovereignty.

continue-judicial-changes.text: That is the party's documented position: on 4 August 2025 the government, whose ministers included the party's, unanimously approved the justice minister's proposal to dismiss the attorney general. The party's plan of 22 September 2026 adds a Knesset hearing and a two-thirds majority for Supreme Court candidates, and defines matters that are not subject to judicial review.

broad-agreed-constitutional-framework.text: The party's documented approach is to give elected officials more power over the courts and the attorney general: the party's plan of 22 September 2026 includes dismissing the attorney general and requiring a Knesset hearing and a two-thirds majority for Supreme Court candidates. The 2022 coalition agreement did also commit all coalition factions to support bills on a Basic Law: Legislation and an override clause.

repeal-changes-protect-independence.text: The party holds the opposite position: on 4 August 2025 the government, whose ministers included the party's, unanimously approved the proposal to dismiss the attorney general. The party's plan of 22 September 2026 proposes changes to how judges are chosen and to the High Court's powers.

keep-current-system-stability.text: The party holds a different position: its plan of 22 September 2026 proposes dismissing the attorney general when the government forms, a Knesset hearing and a two-thirds majority for Supreme Court candidates, and defining matters not subject to judicial review.

state-commission-under-existing-law.text: The party opposes this model: at the government meeting of 16 November 2025, which decided against a state commission of inquiry, National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir said the framework should include no people from the legal system, because those who sit on the bench are part of those being investigated.

commission-appointed-by-knesset-balance.text: The research places the party here mainly on statements: on 16 November 2025, when the government chose a commission reflecting broad agreement over a state commission of inquiry, National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir said the framework should include no people from the legal system. The party's position on the specific commission bills could not be confirmed from Knesset vote records.

commission-chosen-by-neutral-mechanism.text: The party shares your view that the legal system should be among those investigated: on 16 November 2025 National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir said those who sit on the bench are part of those being investigated. But it supports a framework with no people from the legal system, and the research places it closest to members picked through the Knesset rather than by a neutral method.

strengthen-jewish-character.text: The research places the party closest to your answer, but only tentatively, on limited evidence: the Israel Democracy Institute lists bringing Jewish religious law into the legal system among the party's initiatives, and as National Security Minister, in charge of the police, Itamar Ben Gvir has repeatedly said his policy is to allow Jewish prayer on the Temple Mount. No documented party positions were found on civil marriage, conversion rules or public transport on Shabbat.

keep-status-quo.text: The research found no documented party position on civil marriage, conversion rules or public transport on Shabbat, so none on keeping the current arrangements. The tentative indication points toward a larger role for Jewish law and Jewish practice in public life.

more-choice-local-decisions.text: The research found no documented party position on civil marriage, conversion rules or public transport on Shabbat, so none on what this option proposes. The tentative indication points toward a larger role for Jewish law and Jewish practice in public life.

separate-religion-and-state.text: The research found no documented party position on civil marriage, conversion rules or public transport on Shabbat, so none on what this option proposes. The tentative indication points toward a larger role for Jewish law and Jewish practice in public life.

points.text: The party advocates the death penalty for terrorists: the Death Penalty for Terrorists Law, initiated by party MK Limor Son Har-Melech, passed its third reading on 30 March 2026 by 62 to 48, with all six of the party's MKs who voted supporting it.

The party advocates wider private gun licensing: after the October 7 attack in 2023 the ministry of National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir widened eligibility for gun licences, and for 2026 the party campaigns on expanding permits to set up a thousand civilian readiness squads.

The party backs tougher terror-related laws: on 7 November 2024 the Knesset passed by 61 to 41 a law allowing the deportation of first-degree relatives of attackers who knew of an attack in advance and did not report it, or who expressed support for it, and all the party's MKs recorded in the vote supported it.
